newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Iskratel says 1996 net up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Iskratel says 1996 net up 15 pct.

text.p: Slovenian telephone switchboard maker Iskratel, 48-percent owned by Germany's Siemens, said on Monday 1996 net profit rose 15 percent to 3.9 million marks ($2.3 million) as exports surged.
The company said sales rose 22 percent to 171 million marks, while exports were up 24 percent at 113 million marks.

"We expect to increase exports to 80 percent of our production this year, from 66 percent in 1996, while total sales are expected to rise to about 180 million marks in 1997," finance director Metod Zaplotnik told Reuters.
He said half of Isktratel's exports went to Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, while the company also sold to Macedonia, Yugoslavia, Bosnia, Turkey and Germany.
The firm was formed in 1989 as a joint-venture between Siemens and 11 Slovenian banks and companies.
